newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-David Jones year sales ease 0.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-David Jones year sales ease 0.4 pct.

text.p: Retailer David Jones Ltd said on Tuesday 52-week sales to July 26, 1997 came in at A$1.437 billion, against A$1.443 billion last year.
This represented a 0.4 percent decline, and a 3.2 percent decline on a comparable stores basis.
However, David Jones said retail conditions were more favourable in the fourth quarter.
In the 13 weeks to July 26, sales were A$364.2 million, against A$352.6 million a year earlier, a rise of 3.3 percent, or 2.1 percent on a comparable stores basis.
Sales from the David Jones stores were A$341.6 million, up 6.4 percent, while sales from the three John Martin stores were A$22.5 million, down 28.7 percent.
After adjusting for the closure of the Elizabeth store in South Australia, John Martin sales declined 25 percent.
David Jones said better performing product groups in the fourth quarter were women's apparel, shoes and accessories and homeware.

"It was pleasing to see the improvement in sales in the fourth quarter and we hope that this is a sign that the retail climate is improving," David Jones chief executive Peter Wilkinson said in a statement.
David Jones in March reported a 50 percent fall in net profit for the first half to A$22.34 million, and said the year net profit would be lower than in the previous year.
